title: The Beatles: Fab Four
description: Five levels through the band that changed pop music—and the world.

questions.question: John Lennon first met Paul McCartney at a 1957 church fête in Woolton, a suburb of which city?
questions.hint: A port city in northwest England
questions.explanation: On July 6, 1957, 15-year-old Paul borrowed John's guitar, retuned it, and tore through Eddie Cochran's 'Twenty Flight Rock,' knowing every word. John was impressed.

questions.question: After rising from Liverpool, which 1963 breakout single gave its name to their debut album?
questions.explanation: Lennon wrote it as a slow Roy Orbison–style ballad. George Martin sped it up, then told them, "Gentlemen, you've just made your first number one"—though one chart said No. 2.

questions.question: Their debut LP borrowed the 'Please Please Me' title—in how many days did they record its ten new songs?
questions.explanation: On Feb. 11, 1963, they cut 10 songs in under 13 hours for about £400. Last came 'Twist and Shout,' nailed on the first take by a cold-ridden Lennon; after, swallowing felt "like sandpaper."

questions.question: Before that one-day album, who first saw them at Liverpool's Cavern Club in 1961 and became their manager?
questions.explanation: He ran the NEMS record shop around the corner, put them in suits, and taught them their deep stage bow. Paul's verdict: "If anyone was the fifth Beatle, it was Brian."

questions.question: Two years after Epstein's 1967 death, which album became the last one all four Beatles recorded together?
questions.explanation: Recorded after the Let It Be sessions but released first. Its working title was 'Everest,' after engineer Geoff Emerick's cigarettes—until they skipped the Himalayas and shot the cover outside.
